subject: Observability playbook and handoff: dashboards, tracing, and alert routing for MeridianPay
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@meridianpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-07-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Observability playbook and handoff: dashboards, tracing, and alert routing for MeridianPay

Hi Jordan —

Great to meet on Friday. Per our call, attaching a first-pass of the onboarding artifacts so your infra and SRE teams have something to react to during the week: an onboarding map, a runbook template, and a proposed alert-routing matrix.

High-level asks from Redwood:
- Confirm the team that will own dashboards (names/emails) and access level for the Console.
- Share the top 10 business transactions you want instrumented for latency traces (we've seeded a candidate list).
- Point us at current incident channels (PagerDuty team IDs, Slack channel names).

What's attached:
- meridianpay-observability-map.pdf (diagram: data flow, where Redwood telemetry will land)
- redwood-runbook-template.md (example runbook sections + escalation logic)
- alert-routing-proposal.csv (suggested dedupe and severity mapping)

Proposed next steps:
1) Can we lock a 60-min technical walkthrough on Tue 2029-07-23 10:00 PT?
2) If you can share the list of business transactions by EOD Tue we will prepare tracing instrumentation suggestions and SLO targets.

Note: Ben will call out a couple of kernel-level tracing defaults we recommend (sampling and prefix caching) in a follow-up — those are low-risk, high-impact for median latency.

Thanks —
Soojin
Soojin Lee

Thanks Soojin — this looks good. A few quick notes from our side:

1) Dashboard ownership: Ops will own the SLO dashboards (ops-dash@meridianpay.com) and Payments PMs will own the business-metric dashboards (payments-pm@meridianpay.com).
2) Top transactions for tracing: authorization, settlement, refund, recurring-batch, tokenization, 3DS flow, payouts-create, payouts-settle, reconciliation-batch, webhook-delivery. We'll finalize the canonical names and send them by EOD Mon.
3) Incident channels: pagers: PD team id 3271 (ops-oncall), Slack #sre-ops for playbook chatter.

Quick questions before the walkthrough:
- For alert dedupe, can Redwood map alerts to our PD team IDs automatically, or do we need to supply a webhook?
- We have some existing upstream filters that drop noisy 5xx spikes during deploys — can Redwood ingest suppression windows?

We can do Tue 2029-07-23 10:00 PT; adding Aisha and infra-team.

Cheers,
Jordan
Director, Site Reliability Engineering
MeridianPay

Subject: RE: Observability playbook and handoff: dashboards, tracing, and alert routing for MeridianPay

Hey all — quick technical complements ahead of Tue's session.

Jordan — answers inline to your questions:

> For alert dedupe, can Redwood map alerts to our PD team IDs automatically, or do we need to supply a webhook?

We support both modes. Two options:
- If you supply PD team IDs and we get a one-time service-account token, we can push incidents into PD and annotate the PD incident with Redwood's model+route that fired.
- Alternatively, we can forward webhook payloads to a customer-owned ingestion endpoint; that path is preferred if you want to funnel through existing on-prem enrichment.

> We have upstream filters that drop noisy 5xx spikes during deploys — can Redwood ingest suppression windows?

Yes — we call those temporary suppression windows. You can: (a) push a suppression via API with a TTL (we'll surface on the Console), or (b) we can ingest annotations from your deploy system (e.g., Jenkins/Spinnaker tags) and map them automatically to alert suppression. For Monday's walkthrough, please bring one sample deploy annotation so we can demo mapping.

Tech recommendations I'm preparing for Tue:
- Tracing sampling: target 5% tail sampling on p95-sensitive flows (authorization) and higher sampling for payments-pm flows (20%) to support root-cause analysis.
- KV/prefix cache: enable for tokenization and 3DS flows to reduce repeated decoder compute on hot paths.
- Alert routing: we'll propose a two-tier dedupe: group alerts by fingerprint (error signature + route) then route to PD with severity override rules from your alert-routing CSV.

I'll attach a short snippet of the proposed tracer config during the meeting.

Thanks,
Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: tracer-config-snippet.txt (small)
From: Aisha Roy <aisha.roy@meridianpay.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Observability playbook and handoff: dashboards, tracing, and alert routing for MeridianPay

Thanks everyone — the walkthrough went well. Follow-ups we agreed on in the meeting:

- Redwood to provision Console viewer access for ops-dash@meridianpay.com and editor access for payments-pm@meridianpay.com.
- Redwood to produce a draft error taxonomy mapping (payment_error -> 402/decline, gateway_error -> 502/timeout, signature_mismatch -> 401) by EOD Thu 2029-07-25.
- MeridianPay to share one sample deploy annotation and the PD service account token by Fri 2029-07-26.
- Redwood to add a canary alert rule for tokenization latency (p95 > 800ms over 3 min) scoped to canary traffic only.

A couple of notes from infra team during the call: please keep the initial tracer footprint small (Ben's 5% recommendation) and surface the Console cost estimator for sampling changes so we can approve budget impact.

We'll track the follow-ups in the hubspot deal and the drive folder you created. Thanks for the clear runbook template — should speed our internal reviews.

— Aisha
Staff SRE, MeridianPay
